nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis and Calcination
nodes.procedure: Ti mesh (3 cm × 2 cm) was cleaned by sonication sequentially in acetone, water, and ethanol for 10 min each. Co(NO3)2·6H2O (0.291 g), NH4F (0.093 g), and urea (0.30 g) were dissolved in 20 mL water under vigorous stirring for 30 min. Then the solution was transferred into a Teflon-lined stainless autoclave (25 mL), and the cleaned Ti mesh was immersed into the solution. The autoclave was sealed and maintained at 120 °C for 6 h in an electric oven. After the autoclave cooled down slowly at room temperature, the Ti was taken out and washed with water, and then heated at 350 °C for 120 min in a static Ar atmosphere to obtain CoO/Ti.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoO shows diffraction peaks at 36.5°, 42.4°, 61.5°, 73.6°, and 77.5° indexed to (111), (200), (220), (311), and (222) planes of CoO phase (JCPDS no. 71-1178). Co-B@CoO shows additional broad peak at 45.8° assigned to amorphous Co-B phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1A presents the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of CoO and Co-B@CoO scratched down from Ti mesh. Before NaBH₄ treatment, the precursor shows diffraction peaks at 36.5°, 42.4°, 61.5°, 73.6°, and 77.5°, which can be indexed as the (111), (200), (220), (311), and (222) planes of CoO phase, respectively (JCPDS no. 71-1178). After boronation, the broad peak centered at 45.8° in XRD pattern is assigned to amorphous Co-B phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoO/Ti shows array of nanowires 80-100 nm in diameter and several μm in length covering Ti mesh surface. Co-B@CoO/Ti retains 1D nanowire morphology with nanoparticles formed on nanowire surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1B,C shows the SEM images of CoO/Ti, indicating the whole surface of Ti mesh is covered by array of CoO nanowires about 80-100 nm in diameters and several micrometers in length. The treated nanoarray still retains its 1D morphology with the same nanowire length and perfect integration, as shown in Figure 1E and Figure S4 (Supporting Information). A close view of such nanowire reveals the formation of nanoparticles on its surface (Figure 1F).

nodes.characterization_summary: CoO nanowires show single-crystalline structure by SAED. Co-B@CoO shows nanoparticles 10-35 nm diameter on nanowires; Co-B is amorphous by HRTEM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM analysis provides another piece of clear evidence to confirm the development of nanoparticles with diameters in the range of 10-35 nm on nanowire, as shown Figure 1H. High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image taken from such nanoparticle (Figure 1I) reveals that such Co-B is amorphous in nature.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-B@CoO/Ti confirms presence of Co, B, and O elements with Co/B atomic ratio of about 1:0.53. STEM-EDX mapping shows Co-B layer 15-40 nm thick.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectrum of Co-B@CoO/Ti confirms the presence of Co, B, and O elements with a Co/B atomic ratio of about 1:0.53 (Figure S5, Supporting Information). The scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) image and the corresponding EDX elemental mapping images further suggest that the Co-B layer is about 15-40 nm in thickness (Figure 1G).

properties.description: SEM images of nanostructure with scale bar 500 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: CoO shows Co 2p peaks at 786.60, 803.69, 798.01 eV for high-spin Co²⁺. Co-B@CoO shows Co 2p at 781.02 eV (low reduction state Co) and 785.5 eV (CoO), B 1s at 188.2 eV (elemental B, Co₂B) and 192.1 eV (oxidized B). Co/B atomic ratio 1.15:0.61.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2A shows the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) Co 2p core-level spectrum of CoO. Two peaks at 786.60 and 803.69 eV can be assigned to the shakeup excitation of the high-spin Co²⁺... The B 1s core-level XPS spectrum of Co-B@CoO is shown in Figure 2C. Two peaks are apparent at 188.2 and 192.1 eV, corresponding to elemental and oxidized B 1s levels, respectively, suggesting the formation of Co₂B.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-B@CoO has Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 87.3 m² g⁻¹ and larger pore volume with pores ~2.5 and 4 nm. CoO has 70.7 m² g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As determined by nitrogen adsorption/desorption isotherm (Figure 5A) at 77.3 K, the Co-B@CoO has Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of 87.3 m² g⁻¹, which is larger than that of CoO (70.7 m² g⁻¹). Besides, Co-B@CoO also has larger pore volume with pores about 2.5 and 4 nm in size (Figure 5A inset).

nodes.characterization_summary: Double layer capacitance measured from non-faradaic CV (5-200 mV s⁻¹, 0.03-0.13 V vs RHE) gives Cdl = 29.8 mF cm⁻² for Co-B@CoO/Ti (ECSA = 16.0 cm²_ECSA) and 2.9 mF cm⁻² for CoO/Ti (ECSA = 1.56 cm²_ECSA), vs 1.86 mF cm⁻² for bare Ti mesh.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on the cyclic voltammograms at various scan rates (5-200 mV s⁻¹) between 0.03 and 0.13 V versus RHE (Figure S20, Supporting Information), where the current response are only due to the charging of the double layer, the specific capacitances for Co-B@CoO/Ti, CoO/Ti, and bare Ti mesh are determined as 29.8, 2.9, and 1.86 mF cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-B@CoO/Ti shows charge transfer resistance Rct with semidiameter 17 Ω, smaller than CoO/Ti (48 Ω), indicating faster reaction kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy analysis concludes that the R_ct in the Nyquist plot for Co-B@CoO/Ti is much smaller than that of CoO/Ti (Figure S22, Supporting Information), suggesting a lower charge-transfer resistance of Co-B@CoO/Ti and thus markedly faster reaction kinetics.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-B loading 2.50 mg cm⁻², CoO loading 2.37 mg cm⁻². Post-OER electrolysis shows almost unchanged Co:B atomic ratio.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to ICP-AES results, the amounts for Co-B and CoO are 2.50 and 2.37 mg cm⁻², respectively. Inductively coupled plasma atom emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) analysis further gives almost unchanged Co:B atomic ratio, implying the formation of oxide/hydroxide layer did not alter initial stoichiometry of the catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED patterns from different areas of CoO nanowires confirm single-crystalline CoO structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns taken from different areas of the nanowire further suggest the formation of single-crystalline CoO structure, as shown in Figure 1D and Figure S3 (Supporting Information).
